text:
incident-bot: P0 — Multiple inference pods reporting crashes and node reboots in us-west-3. Automatic alert: GPU driver resets and ECC parity warnings spiking across a subset of nodes. Paging oncall.

carmen (oncall): saw the alert, grabbing it now. any obvious customer-facing impact?

devon (sre): yes, some 503s and timeouts from hosted-inference API over last 7m. Tracing shows requests hitting a small set of nodes that are flapping. Metrics: token throughput down ~28% in the zone.

maria (support): we have two customers on live sessions complaining about token truncation and reconnects. I'll open a bridge if impact grows.

incident-bot: Recent NVML logs: ``
[  125.456789] NVRM: GPU 3: Xid 62 detected, GPU has fallen off the bus
[  125.456799] nvidia 0000:03:00.0: GPU at PCI:0000:03:00: GPU has fallen off the bus
[  125.457012] kernel: [drm] *ERROR* GPU stall detected, recovery initiated
``

devon (sre): Xid 62 / ECC parity spike. Looking at dmesg there's repeated driver resets and one kernel oops on node aws-uw3-gpu-12. Posting short kernel excerpt: 
```
[ 128.123456] kernel: NVRM: GPU 0: Xid 62, GPU hang detected
[ 128.123460] kernel: Out of memory: kill process 14233 (serve-infer) score 124 or sacrifice child
[ 128.123470] kernel: Killed process 14233 (serve-infer) total-vm:512000kB, anon-rss:410000kB
```

carmen (oncall): ok plan: cordon + drain affected hosts, fallback routing to dedicated pool, and raise telemetry. can we automate the initial cordon for the worst nodes?

ryan (platform): yes — I can push a short routing rule: route inference traffic away from us-west-3 nodes tagged unstable->dedicated-pool. will flip in ~1m. Also suggest throttling high-concurrency models to reduce memory pressure.

devon (sre): running targeted ops now. commands I ran: 
```
kubectl cordon aws-uw3-gpu-12
kubectl drain aws-uw3-gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
kubectl annotate node aws-uw3-gpu-12 redwood/unstable=parity-flicker
```
Those drains completed for two nodes, one node hit pod eviction timeout due to local-data; I'll forcibly delete the stuck pods next.

ops-bot: action: node aws-uw3-gpu-12 cordoned by devon (sre) at 2508123475

maria (support): opened incident bridge for customers CC list and sent initial status: "We are observing transient GPU driver resets causing reconnects; teams are actively mitigating — will update in 15m."

devon (sre): telemetry note: kernel oops frequency correlates with a firmware roll earlier in the fleet (fw v2.1.9). I'm seeing ECC corrected error counts rising then bursts of uncorrectable parity. Dumping ECC counters: 
```
# nvidia-smi --query-gpu=ecc.errors.uncorrected,ecc.errors.corrected --format=csv
GPU 0, 12, 180
GPU 1, 0, 4
GPU 2, 9, 130
GPU 3, 42, 890  <-- problematic
```
This suggests hardware-level instability on GPU 3 class across a handful of hosts.

carmen (oncall): decision log: 1) isolate (cordon + drain) any node with uncorrected ECC > 10; 2) set routing fallback to dedicated pool; 3) if driver resets persist after node eviction, escalate to hardware replacement and customer comps queue.

ryan (platform): routing change pushed and verified. Traffic for high-throughput tenants moved to dedicated-pool-us-west. Fallback successful: error rate dropped ~60% for affected customers.

devon (sre): I’m forcing pod deletes on the stuck pods and restarting node-level nvidia-driver service to see if soft-recovery helps before full reprovision. Command: 
```
sudo systemctl restart nvidia-docker.service || sudo modprobe -r nvidia && sudo modprobe nvidia
journalctl -u nvidia-docker -n 200 --no-pager | tail -n 50
```
If process keeps hitting OOM kills during restarts, we’ll reprovision instance.

maria (support): note for comms: one customer (acme-analytics) reported 1m30s of degraded sessions with reconnects. I've flagged for SLA review and asked for logs.

devon (sre): quick mitigation update: 3 of 5 affected nodes cordoned/drained; two nodes recovered after driver restart, one node continued to exhibit Xid 62 bursts and a sustained uncorrected ECC counter — taking it out of rotation permanently and opening hardware replacement ticket with cloud.

incident-bot: severity remains P0. Suggested post-incident actions: firmware/driver audit for v2.1.9, expand ECC telemetry alert thresholds, and add automated node isolation when uncorrected ECC exceeds threshold.

carmen (oncall): agreed. I'll file the RCA ticket and tag research for kernel/driver analysis. Maria — keep customers updated, call if any bridge needed. Ryan — coordinate with accounts for dedicated replacements if hardware swap requires maintenance window.

maria (support): sending updated email to impacted list now. will add note about fallback to dedicated pool and expected next update in 30m. :white_check_mark:

devon (sre): final ops note: left the following K8s annotation on removed nodes for postmortem: "redwood/incident-2508123456=isolated-ecc-uncorrected>10". Recording timestamped logs and core dumps to artifacts bucket s3://redwood-incident-logs/2508123456/.

carmen (oncall): handing off to follow-up rotation. I'll drop a summary in the incident tracker. Oncall moving to next incident in 10m.

ops-bot: handoff: carmen -> oncall-followup at 2508123600

maria (support): I'll keep the bridge open until replacement is scheduled. closing active paging for now but monitoring.
